title: I’d recommend anyone buy this app if they detest complexity in their organization

As someone who for the longest time kept their list of personal and professional tasks in a large notebook with dog eared pages running about it, this app helps to digitize that and keep it well organized.

author: Fantastic ;)

title: Work on all levels.
body:
I heard about the goblin tool on an ADHD FB group and I’m so happy I did! 

I’ve been using it for over a month now, mostly to break down tasks into manageable steps. Which is *chef’s kiss*. The levels of spiciness are fabulous and each task can then be broken down. Brilliant!! 

I recently used it to interpret texts I was receiving. Thank you, Goblin Tools, for also seeing the passive aggressive voice in them. This helped me to step back and take a breath. I was able to formulate an answer in my own words, but if I wasn’t able to there’s a spot for that in this nifty tool as well! Want to be less or spicy? Formal, informal, oh polite. This app has you covered. 

Thank you to the brilliant app designers. I’m less fatigued at the end of the day while working on bettering my executive functioning abilities. 

Btw I haven’t even tried out the “give me a meal ideas to make with these ingredients” cooking section yet!? I know!? It’s like those “but wait there’s more” ads. 

Try out this tool - neurospicy or not - it’s a gem!

There’s more that’s awesome, but I for one am deeply grateful that the goblin behind these tools created this app. It’s does the things with AI that I would have asked C3PO for help with! 🙏❤️

title: So far so good
body:
I’ve been using this app for about a week now. I really like how it breaks down tasks so well. Sometimes I’m able to remove some of them and condense the list, which is nice because I found if I got too many items  going on my list it slowed down the app quite a bit. 
Honestly though that isn’t the worst thing, as I tend to try and overdo it with my planning and don’t have enough hours in the day to complete what I want to get done. So the app slowing down with too many tasks has also helped me be a little bit more realistic with myself because I don’t want to overload the app- or myself. An unintended aid I’m sure but I’m appreciating it
I haven’t used the chef portion much yet but that’s the next thing I’m going to be diving into as I feel it will be so beneficial to take some of the thinking away on my part.
Overall I love this app and definitely feel I already got my moneys worth. I’ve told many of my friends with brains that seem to work similar to mine and they all seem as awestruck as I. 
Goblin Tools is a wonderful addition to my toolbox of things to help me get through life ❤️

body: Cheap! 0.99$ and it has many functions. I isn’t cute or too colourful, but it’s simple and works for me.

title: Great for AuDHD
body: I have awful task paralysis, never know where to start with a lot of tasks, and have a tendency to jump from task to task rather than seeing one through. Having tasks broken down into steps alleviated some of the anxiety, and if I’m stuck on a task portion I can break it down even further. Plus a dopamine reward of behind able you cross of steps on my list. Really hoping speech to text will be added soon like it is in the non app version.
author: SpoonieOT

title: No words explain how happy this makes me
body:
Goblin Tools was originally recommended by my therapist because my autism makes managing multiple things super panic-inducing and this app allows me to break them down into very small, easy-to-do steps. It also helps me understand tone and meaning in someone’s text, and a huge one I am excited about it the Chef which writes you a recipe based on any ingredients you owns (like, any).

Bram the developer is like a king for the neurospicies, we love you!!
